findings.title: Trusted time is missing at the actual expiry blocking observation
findings.detail: At reviewed SHA 1df15275291ee99b98bd063e856d45c83ccc6f81, test_trusted_post_lock_expiry obtains before_wait at line 2046 before blocker connection/row acquisition and waiter setup, then observe_blocked records only pid, blocking_pids and query. No trusted DB timestamp is obtained and asserted below the immutable source_end at the actual blocking observation. Consequently the persisted trusted_before_wait < source_end < trusted_after inequality can hold even if the waiter begins waiting after expiry. The exact TIME_INELIGIBLE/expired denial still proves rejection after expiry, but does not prove the packet's required expiry-crossed-during-an-observed-lock-wait oracle. Independently inspected observe_blocked at lines 1044-1056 and all four raw trusted_post_lock_expiry_DC witnesses; their blocking tuples contain no clock observation. This is an evidence/oracle defect, not a request to change production semantics.
findings.requested_action: Obtain fresh trusted database time with the actual pg_blocking_pids observation and require observed_blocked_at < immutable source_end before holding the blocker across expiry. Persist that observation and the post-release denial for all four T6/START/CONTINUE/RESUME cases. Fail or safely reconstruct a new owner trajectory if setup misses the bound; do not edit persisted expiry or inject caller time. Rerun all exact packet checks on a new tested commit and obtain fresh reviews.
